extracted.intended_audience: public information officers (PIOs), government communications staff, and local/state/federal agency press officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting official government press releases (municipal, county, state, federal) that inform media and the public about policies, programs, emergencies, appointments, and use of public funds while maintaining public accountability and neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should be informational, not promotional, written in third person, using plain language, avoiding political spin and maintaining neutral framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use factual, neutral wording; avoid advocacy or promotional language. Keep third-person voice and plain-language phrasing suitable for broad public audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline states the news in plain language and avoids vague or promotional phrasing so the reader knows exactly what happened from the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the headline specific and informative — convey the main event or announcement clearly. Avoid buzzwords, marketing-style hooks, or ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening Paragraph (Lead)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead paragraph answers who, what, when, where, why in 2-3 sentences; everything essential up front and include impact on citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the most important facts in the first 2–3 sentences (5 Ws). Explicitly state how the announcement affects residents or stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body
rubrics_metrics.description: Body provides background and context, specific data and statistics, officials' quotes, historical context if relevant, and comparisons to baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize supporting details after the lead: include verifiable statistics, context that explains the significance, and authorized quotes that add perspective. Use comparisons (baselines/trends) where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief description of the issuing department/agency including mission, size, location, and achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep boilerplate short and standard across releases so media can easily reuse agency description; include mission and contactable facts about the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Government Press Release Components
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential structural elements that should appear on a government press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE"; agency letterhead/seal; date; headline; subheadline; dateline; lead paragraph (5 Ws); body with quotes from officials; statistical/factual support; action items for citizens (if applicable); department description; contact info for PIO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear public benefit/impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should clearly convey the public benefit or impact of the news or action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain who benefits or is affected, and in what way — prioritize clarity on outcomes for citizens rather than organizational self-interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate facts and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: All factual assertions and statistics included must be accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite sources where appropriate; double-check numbers and dates. Provide context for statistics (denominators, timeframes) to avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes from authorized officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes from authorized officials (mayor, agency head, etc.) to provide voice and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quotes are from properly authorized spokespeople and add perspective or explanation rather than repeating facts verbatim. Keep quotes concise and purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language (Grade 8 reading level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain language suitable for about an 8th-grade reading level so information is accessible to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon, technical terms, and long sentences. Use short paragraphs and clear verbs; consider readability checks and plain-language editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No partisan framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases must avoid partisan framing and political spin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame content around public service, facts, and neutral description of policy or action — do not use messaging that promotes party or candidate interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: All affected populations identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify all populations affected by the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about who is impacted (demographics, geographic areas, program-eligible groups) so audiences understand relevance and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action steps for citizens (if needed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include clear, actionable instructions or next steps for citizens when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide simple, step-by-step guidance, deadlines, locations, links, and any eligibility criteria. Highlight urgent actions (e.g., evacuation steps) prominently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency contact for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact information for the public information officer (PIO) or other agency contact for media and citizen follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, phone number, email, and preferred contact hours. Ensure contact is authorized and prepared to respond to inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible to all (translated if needed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make releases accessible to all audiences, including translation when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide translations for languages spoken by affected communities, consider alternative formats for accessibility (large print, plain text), and ensure digital postings meet accessibility standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliant with FOIA/public records standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases must comply with Freedom of Information Act and public records rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that drafts, emails, and records relating to releases may be public records; follow agency records retention and disclosure policies and avoid including nonpublic deliberative content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checked for accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases should be fact-checked prior to distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify names, titles, dates, figures, and legal citations. Use internal verification processes and require sign-off from subject-matter experts when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved through proper channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases must be approved through the agency's established review and authorization process before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow internal sign-off procedures (legal review, policy offices, executives) and document approvals to ensure accountability and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency releases: brief, action-focused, frequent updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency releases should be concise, focused on actions citizens must take, and updated frequently as the situation evolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize life-safety information, clear instructions, and rapid distribution. Use repeated updates to correct or expand information; coordinate with emergency management entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy releases: background, rationale, implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy announcements should include background information, the rationale for the policy, and implementation details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context for why the policy is being adopted, implementation timelines, responsible parties, and implications for affected groups. Anticipate common questions and address them in the release or FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award/recognition releases: standard congratulatory format
rubrics_metrics.description: Award or recognition releases follow a standard congratulatory format highlighting accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name recipients, describe the achievement or award, include quotations and context, and provide information on any next steps (e.g., ceremonies). Keep tone celebratory but factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response: acknowledgment, action, accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis-response releases should acknowledge the issue, state actions being taken, and communicate accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about what is known and unknown, outline immediate and planned responses, provide resources for affected parties, and identify contact points for media and public inquiries.
